plans.note: Section 7 is captioned 'LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR' and is the operative cap provision. Check whether the cap is mutual or protects Contractor only, whether the amount is tied to fees paid, and whether carve-outs (IP infringement, confidentiality, gross negligence/willful misconduct, indemnity obligations) survive the cap. A one-sided cap plus a consequential-damages waiver running only in RadialSpark's favour is a material deviation.

The heading signals indemnification running to the Contractor (us indemnifying RadialSpark), i.e., the wrong direction. Confirm whether any Vendor-side IP/misconduct indemnity exists here or in sec-5 (reps and warranties); if only a Customer indemnity appears, treat as a directional deviation and note the absent Vendor IP indemnity rather than double-flagging under LOL-CAP.

No covenants/restrictive-covenant section in the outline. Any restriction on Clear Capital's business would most plausibly sit in sec-1 (Purpose of Engagement) as a scope limitation. Also check the unlisted section 2, which is not in the supplied outline. Presence rule: flag only if an actual restriction on our business appears.

Look for exclusive-engagement language in sec-1 (Purpose) or a fee provision in sec-3 conditioning compensation on routing all work through Contractor. Gap at section 2 should be reviewed if the full text becomes available; otherwise treat as absent.

Pricing terms live in sec-3 (Contractor's Compensation); an MFN obliging us to give RadialSpark our best terms would appear there. Nothing in the outline suggests one. Directional rule: an MFN in our favour is welcome and must not be flagged.

No confidentiality/personnel section listed. A no-hire binding Clear Capital, if present, would most likely be tucked into sec-1 or the termination provisions in sec-6. Check duration, scope and whether a general-advertising/unsolicited-response carve-out exists before flagging.

Section 6 (Termination) is the sole candidate. Verify we have a convenience right on reasonable notice without early-termination fees or forfeiture of prepaid amounts, and that RadialSpark cannot terminate for convenience mid-engagement. Interaction with sec-3 compensation (wind-down fees) should be read together.

No term/renewal section appears in the outline; term mechanics may sit in sec-6 or in the unlisted section 2. If an auto-renewal exists, check the non-renewal notice window and any uplift cap; a missing uplift cap alone is a rationale note, not a deviation.

No general/miscellaneous provisions section is listed, so governing law and venue may be absent from the supplied outline. Check the preamble for entity/state recitals and the tail of sec-7. NY, DE, CA or England and Wales are acceptable; an accepted-but-not-preferred forum is a rationale note only.

No miscellaneous section in the outline; assignment/change-of-control language, if any, would likely attach to sec-6 (Termination) as a termination trigger. Flag only if RadialSpark can terminate or withhold consent on our change of control, or if our affiliate/successor assignment is blocked.

Section 4 (Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance) is the core IP provision. Confirm deliverables vest in Clear Capital on payment (or on creation), that our pre-existing IP and data are not assigned or licensed to Contractor beyond performing the Services, and check how the acceptance mechanic interacts with sec-3 payment triggers.

Any licence-back or retained-tools licence from RadialSpark should sit in sec-4 alongside ownership. Check that the grant extends to our affiliates and contractors and is not revocable at will; if sec-4 is a pure assignment with no residual licence, note that rather than flagging.

An audit of Clear Capital's usage or records would most plausibly be a compensation-verification right in sec-3. Nothing in the outline indicates one. If present, test frequency, notice, off-site preference and who bears cost.

Check sec-3 for late-payment interest, penalties or forfeiture payable by us, and sec-7 for any stipulated-damages language. Directional rule: credits or damages payable to us are fine; only amounts payable by Clear Capital are flagged. Ordinary late-payment interest at a commercial rate is a rationale note.

Section 5 pairs Contractor warranties with a warranty disclaimer. Confirm a workmanlike/conformity-to-Specifications warranty with a stated duration and a real remedy (re-perform or refund), and check that the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty. Read with sec-4's acceptance mechanic, which may be the practical remedy.

No insurance section in the outline; if any coverage covenant exists it would ride with sec-5 reps or the risk-allocation language in sec-7. Given Contractor performs Services and may touch our data, treat as missing and note the standard coverage set.

Section 3 (Contractor's Compensation) is where any minimum fee, retainer or take-or-pay commitment would appear. A fixed retainer that is refundable or terminable on notice under sec-6 is acceptable; flag only a true minimum-volume commitment with no exit.

Check sec-6 for post-termination obligations and sec-4 for delivery/return of work product and Clear Capital materials. If neither provides for return of our data and wind-down assistance at agreed rates, treat as missing.
